reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.body: I have explored the Archive with a browser occasionally over several years. Last week, I found your app for iPhone. I now have dark circles under my eyes. I can't watch it all at once but I am trying to with the vintage classic cartoons. (Some cartoon studios lost their copyrights for various reasons.) The app itself is excellent. Its small size puts other streaming apps to shame. The only improvement I can suggest is to reorganize the More menu for identifying serial episodes with a numerical index. For example, Spy Smasher (1942) series. I am currently watching the Anderson's UFO (1969) series of 26 episodes at 50 minutes each. I am going by whatever default sort but only seeing file type and size. Sorting options would help. Even an artificial index would be an improvement. I collected Buck Rogers (1939), and have a list of hundreds of vintage animations. Pat Sullivan's Felix the Cat series, and Mutt & Jeff series. Burt Gillett's Molly-Moo Cow series. Ted Eshbaugh's Goofy Goat (1931) series, and The Abominable Snowman. Harman & Ising's Bosko series from Looney Tunes. Van Beuren's Cubby Bear series, and the original Tom & Jerry series (two optimistic guys during the Depression).…

reviews.body: this app is a really good way to view films from the Archive. it's a simple design but that it actually a plus for it. I like playing stuff, while I listen to something else, like educational podcasts, or old radio shows. great for media preservation and I greatly thank the person or people that work on this, for seemingly free. preserve our history before ignorance burns it all away. they used to burn film reels after showing long enough, to save space. Dr who episodes have been lost that way

reviews.title: I’ve always wanted this!
reviews.body: Works really well. Interface is intuitive and the feature set is absolutely bonkers. Curated channels? Random modes? A clip editor for sharing? Direct link to donate and support archive.org?? Unreal!! I’ve been wanting to make something like this for a long time. Before attempting to tackle this with AI (I have a life outside development lol) I figured I’d search again for something someone already made, and here it is. Thank you.
